title: The Two Seas and the Most Merciful's Servants

paragraphs.text: Allah spreads the rain among people so they may remember, but most refuse and only disbelieve. If He willed, He could have sent a warner to every city. So the Prophet should not obey the disbelievers, but strive against them with the Quran.

Allah let two seas flow side by side. One is fresh and sweet, and the other is salty and bitter. He placed a barrier between them. He created human beings from water and gave them family ties through birth and marriage. Yet people worship what can neither help nor harm them. The Prophet was sent only to give good news and to warn. He asks no payment, only that people take a way to their Lord. Trust in the Ever-Living, who never dies. Allah created the heavens and earth in six days, then rose above the Throne. When told to bow to the Most Merciful, the disbelievers ask, "Who is the Most Merciful?" This makes them turn away more. Allah placed great stars, a burning lamp and a shining moon in the sky. He made night and day follow each other for those who want to remember or be thankful.

The servants of the Most Merciful walk on the earth gently. When foolish people speak rudely to them, they reply with peace. They spend the night bowing and standing in prayer. They ask Allah to keep away the punishment of Hell. When they spend, they are neither wasteful nor stingy, but moderate.

hardWords.m: not wanting to spend or give
in the middle, not too much or too little
